section_summary: The section centers on foreign-owned perpetual leaseholds in Japan, especially disputes over whether leaseholders must pay income, municipal, and other taxes in addition to ground rent. It includes diplomatic correspondence, a Japanese ordinance establishing a lease commission, surveys of American holdings in Kobe, Yokohama, and Nagasaki, and State Department analyses of possible settlement. Two cross-file reports concern Japanese land settlement and migration.

subfiles.title: Taxation on Incomes Derived from Perpetual Lease Property in Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards the Embassy's reply to Whiting S. Worden about taxes on Yokohama rental income.
subfiles.summary: Grew encloses a letter addressing Worden's income-tax liability.

subfiles.title: Letter to Whiting S. Worden on income from perpetual lease property
subfiles.about: Explains why the Embassy cannot claim treaty protection against income tax on Worden's Yokohama rentals.
subfiles.summary: Grew distinguishes the Hague house-tax award from income taxation and says American perpetual leases are private contracts. The Embassy would consider protesting only if Worden supplied legal evidence of discrimination against Americans.

subfiles.title: Division note on the Japanese Perpetual Lease Commission
subfiles.about: Records receipt of Tokyo's despatch on the new lease commission.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance creates a high-level commission; no Department action is recommended.

subfiles.title: Perpetual Lease Property in Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits the ordinance establishing Japan's Perpetual Lease Commission.
subfiles.summary: Grew outlines the commission's composition and expects any settlement offered to British leaseholders to extend to Americans.

subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 2: Organization of Perpetual Lease Commission
subfiles.about: Establishes a commission to investigate and consider perpetual leases.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Minister chairs the commission; the ordinance specifies its membership, powers, secretaries, and clerks.

subfiles.title: Request for report on the Perpetual Lease Commission and American holdings
subfiles.from: William Phillips, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests developments, settlement views, and an inventory of American perpetual leasehold property.
subfiles.summary: The Department seeks commission updates and names, property counts, and values of American holdings.

subfiles.title: File note for Report No. 125
subfiles.about: Cross-references a Tokyo report on land-settlement plans and practices.
subfiles.summary: Points to file 800.52/11 and the attached Sturgeon report.

subfiles.title: Land-Settlement Plans and Practices in Japan
subfiles.from: Leo D. Sturgeon, American Consulate General, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese government settlement policy in Hokkaido, Karafuto, and Korea.
subfiles.summary: The report says settlement policy chiefly served reclamation, resource development, population relief, and cultural aims rather than direct employment relief. It details land allotments, transport discounts, cash subsidies, and services for migrants in Hokkaido, Karafuto, and Korea, with migration figures and descriptions of Korean settlement societies. It ends with its published and interview sources.

subfiles.title: File note for Report No. 143
subfiles.about: Cross-references a report on internal migration and colonial settlement.
subfiles.summary: Points to file 894.55/4 and a pertinent extract from Report No. 143.

subfiles.title: Internal Migration and Colonial Settlement
subfiles.about: Assesses the limited results of migration to Hokkaido and Sakhalin.
subfiles.summary: The extract cites Sturgeon's earlier report and Darrell H. Davis, reporting falling immigration to Hokkaido and limited settlement in southern Sakhalin despite government incentives.

subfiles.title: Perpetual Leases
subfiles.about: Reports the stalled British-Japanese settlement talks and encloses inventories of American leases.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that Japan rejected cash compensation for converting perpetual leases to fee-simple ownership and that its commission had been inactive. British diplomats feared unilateral cancellation and asked the American Embassy to coordinate before acting. Grew recommends awaiting British deliberations and encloses a conversation memorandum plus consular property surveys.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Sir Robert Clive on perpetual leases
subfiles.about: Records the British Ambassador's request for diplomatic coordination.
subfiles.summary: Clive asks for consultation and suggests a new formula for permanent property tenure.

subfiles.title: American perpetual lease holdings in Kobe
subfiles.about: Lists American-owned perpetual lease lots in Kobe and estimates their value.
subfiles.summary: Donovan lists five lots and estimates land values at ¥400–1,000 per tsubo.

subfiles.title: Status of perpetual leases in Yokohama
subfiles.about: Describes tax demands, protests, and payments by American leaseholders and tenants.
subfiles.summary: Boyce describes uneven American responses to city and prefectural taxes, including payments under protest, interest waivers, and threatened seizures. He reviews individual and corporate owners and encloses a property schedule.

subfiles.title: List of Perpetual Lease Properties in Yokohama
subfiles.about: Itemizes American-owned perpetual lease properties, areas, and estimated values.
subfiles.summary: The schedule lists private, corporate, and missionary holdings in Yokohama, with Standard-Vacuum lots also in Kobe and Nagasaki.

subfiles.title: American Owners of Perpetual Lease Property in Nagasaki
subfiles.about: Transmits a Nagasaki ownership list and explains why values were unavailable.
subfiles.summary: Spamer clarifies ownership and trusteeship but finds reliable sales valuations unobtainable.

subfiles.title: American Owners of Perpetual Lease Property in Nagasaki: list
subfiles.about: Lists Nagasaki lots, owners, areas, occupants, and trustees.
subfiles.summary: The list covers U.S. government, company, mission, private, and Seamen's Home properties.

subfiles.title: Cover note on draft instruction concerning perpetual leaseholds
subfiles.about: Introduces a draft instruction reviewing the leasehold dispute.
subfiles.summary: The note outlines the draft's history, legal analysis, and proposed inquiry to Britain.

subfiles.title: Instruction on perpetual leaseholds in Japan
subfiles.from: William Phillips, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Analyzes American leaseholders' rights and directs consultation on a possible negotiated settlement.
subfiles.summary: The Department reviews nineteenth-century settlement agreements, the 1894 and 1911 treaties, and the Hague house-tax award. It concludes that American holders may demand treatment equal to other foreign holders, but that their claim to broad exemption from municipal taxes is unconvincing. It proposes negotiation over fee-simple titles and future tax obligations, asks the Embassy to learn whether Britain has advanced a plan, and requests Grew's assessment.

subfiles.title: File note on alien immigration and land ownership ordinances
subfiles.about: Cross-references Grew's despatch enclosing translations of two 1899 Japanese ordinances.
subfiles.summary: Points to file 894.55/12 on alien immigration and land ownership.

subfiles.title: The Question of Perpetual Leaseholds in Japan
subfiles.about: Reviews the history, legal arguments, American holdings, and possible equitable settlement of the leasehold dispute.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum traces foreign concessions, ground rents, the 1905 Hague award, and the competing tax claims of leaseholders and Japanese authorities. It contrasts British treaty rights with the American position under the 1911 treaty and Japanese assurances of equal treatment. Tables summarize American properties in Kobe, Yokohama, and Nagasaki; the author argues for a settlement attentive to both vested leaseholder interests and municipal needs. The document continues beyond page 72.
